Copy-paste bug: the second increment line assigns to `sendSegmentNumber` instead of `receiveSegmentNumber`:
```java
sendSegmentNumber = incrementUintSegmentNumber(sendSegmentNumber, 1);
sendSegmentNumber = incrementUintSegmentNumber(receiveSegmentNumber, 1); // ← should be receiveSegmentNumber =
```
As written, `sendSegmentNumber` is incremented twice (the second time with `receiveSegmentNumber`'s value), and `receiveSegmentNumber` is never advanced. The second line should be:
```java
receiveSegmentNumber = incrementUintSegmentNumber(receiveSegmentNumber, 1);
```

The modulo constant is incorrect. `0xFFFFFFFFL` is `2^32 - 1`, but a 32-bit unsigned integer wraps at `2^32`. Using `% 0xFFFFFFFFL` means:
- The valid value `0xFFFFFFFF` (max uint32) is never produced (it maps to `0`).
- The wrap boundary is off by one.
The fix should use either:
```java
return (sequenceNumber + value) & 0xFFFFFFFFL;
```
or equivalently:
```java
return (sequenceNumber + value) % 0x100000000L;
```
The bitwise AND is the more idiomatic way to mask to 32 bits in Java.

review_comment: We should produce a 5G file and try to read it using Wireshark just to be double-sure.
@normanmaurer I'll have time today to look into this and address any issues I find.

Found 2 issues directly related to this PR while using Wireshark to look at the generated 5GB pcap. Those will be addressed.

Noticed two other issues present in 4.1.

1. If the payload is larger than 65495 for TCP, the length field in the IP packet is incorrect due to the length being a ushort. UDP will have a similar problem.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/155cec08-767f-4efc-a2c5-c9c04718bd75)
2. When the PcapWriteHandler is attached to a TCP server, the FIN messages have incorrect segment and ack numbers. 
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/236c3109-558d-4fa2-8cce-5fa05503ebc0)


I will try to find the time to address these here with unit tests

For TCP, the payload can just be split into multiple PCAP entries. 
For UDP, I imagine it could just log that it received too large of a payload.
Alright, all of the above have been handled. Tested large PCAP files and those show correctly in Wireshark now.
